label: Time of day
description: Visible daily phases from predawn and sunrise through daylight, sunset, twilight, and night.
notes: Daily phases belong here, phrased to follow “at.” lighting.natural owns named lighting effects, while scene.weather owns sky conditions and scene.season owns annual changes. Closely spaced clock hours are omitted; the retained phases differ in sky brightness, sun position, shadow length, or the balance of daylight and artificial light. Morning and evening can resemble each other, so their looks describe typical visible cues rather than guaranteed differences.

values.look: The landscape is still dark beneath a deep indigo sky with a faint pale band on the horizon.
The sun first breaks the horizon, casting low peach light across a largely shadowed landscape.
Clear daylight fills the scene, with the sun well above the horizon and slanting shadows.
The sun is high overhead; shadows are short and collect directly beneath objects.
The sun sits lower in a still-bright sky, casting long, sharply defined shadows.
Low amber sunlight warms surfaces and rims silhouettes with gold above long shadows.
The sun touches the horizon under an orange or pink sky, with dark silhouettes in the foreground.
After sunset, a luminous cobalt sky lights the scene while warm windows and streetlights begin to stand out.
The sky has almost gone dark, leaving a thin twilight band while artificial lights dominate the scene.
The sky is fully dark with no twilight glow; moonlight, stars, or isolated lamps reveal the scene.
